title: Graceful disconnect: buffered tool-call retry and reconnect window for streaming API
author: Aisha Khan
description: Motivation: We observed customer incidents where short-lived client disconnects during multi-step function/tool-calling flows caused duplicate tool invocations or orphaned streaming sessions, leading to higher costs and inconsistent structured outputs. This PR introduces a server-side in-flight buffer and a short reconnect window with idempotency reconciliation to preserve end-to-end semantics while keeping latency and cost in check. Summary of changes: 1) Session manager: add a buffered-inflight queue that retains in-progress tool invocations for a configurable reconnect window (default 20s). Sessions now emit a compact session token (reconnect_token) on streaming start. 2) Tool invocation idempotency: introduce X-Tool-Invocation-Id header and runtime-side idempotency table so duplicate replays are deduplicated; tools should return idempotency-safe responses. 3) Reconnect/reconcile flow: upon client reconnect with reconnect_token, server attempts to reconcile buffered inflight work with the client's last-ack position, returning any accumulated partial structured output and the current tool invocation states. If the client reconnects after the window, buffered items are aborted with graceful teardown events. 4) Soft-cancel semantics: new soft-cancel signal allows clients to request an in-flight tool call be aborted only if it has not reached an irreversible side-effect point; otherwise the server completes the call and returns final structured output. 5) SDK/compat: TypeScript and Python SDKs added helper APIs to expose reconnect_token and soft-cancel semantics while preserving OpenAI-compatible streaming events (partial chunks, function_call start/finish events). 6) Observability: new metrics (session.reconnect_attempts, tool.invocation.dedup_hits, session.buffered_items) and traces to aid debugging. 7) Tests: unit tests for reconcile/timeout logic, integration tests simulating flaky client disconnects, and an e2e test that ensures no duplicate tool executions for retries. Checklist: - [x] API design reviewed for OpenAI compatibility - [x] Runtime changes gated behind feature flag streaming_reconnect_v2 - [x] SDK helpers implemented and docstrings added - [x] Metrics and tracing added - [x] Tests included and green on CI Design notes: reconnect_token is short-lived (default TTL 20s) to avoid long-lived server buffering. The buffered queue is size-capped per-session and uses LRU eviction for low-memory impact; overflow causes immediate abort with structured error to client. Soft-cancel is advisory to the runtime and will translate to an AbortableContext inside tool runners; tools can opt-in to fast abort or honor idempotency markers and complete. Compatibility: OpenAI-compatible streaming events are preserved: the server emits a function_call.start event when a tool is invoked, intermittent partial function_call.content chunks during streaming, and function_call.finish when completed; on reconnect the server will stream any missed chunks and then resume new output. CI notes: initial run flagged a flaky e2e test that relied on timing; test was stabilized by switching to event-based waits and re-run. Merge: squash-merged to main on 2026-03-03 after approvals. Impact: reduces duplicate tool calls in flaky network scenarios, gives SDKs a clear reconnect primitive, and improves observability for streaming interruptions. Runtime defaults keep memory/cost bounded and the feature is controlled by feature flags for gradual rollout.
commit_summaries: session: add reconnect token + buffered in-flight queue and TTL logic
runtime: implement tool invocation idempotency table and X-Tool-Invocation-Id header handling
sdk-ts: expose reconnect token and softCancel() helper on StreamingClient
sdk-py: add StreamingClient.reconnect(token) convenience and tests
tests: integration + e2e for reconnect and de-dupe scenarios
docs: streaming reconnect API changes and migration notes
feature-flag: gating streaming_reconnect_v2 behind rollout flag
review_comments: Martin Li: Can we make the reconnect TTL configurable per-deployment? For high-throughput customers 20s may be too short.
Aisha Khan (author): TTL is configurable at deployment level via streaming_reconnect_ttl in the config; default 20s for hosted to limit memory. Added note in docs.
Sofia Ramirez: Please add more asserts to the e2e test that verify no duplicate external tool calls are made (mock the tool endpoint).
Aisha Khan (author): Added tool endpoint mock and assert in e2e. Also added metric that counts dedup hits to make it easier in prod.
Ben Carter: I worry about the LRU eviction semantics leaking user-visible errors in the middle of a flow. Can we emit an explicit structured error event before discarding?
Aisha Khan (author): Good point — we now emit session.buffer_overflow error event with structured error code and include a best-effort partial output snapshot.
release_notes: Introduce a reconnect token and buffered in-flight queue to make streaming sessions resilient to short client disconnects; add tool invocation idempotency markers and SDK helpers for reconnect and soft-cancel behavior. Feature gated behind streaming_reconnect_v2.
